newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean groups pledge fresh corn aid to North.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean groups pledge fresh corn aid to North.

text.p: South Korean civic groups said on Friday they would donate an additional 30,000 tonnes of corn to North Korea to help ease hunger in the north.
Seven religious and other civic groups said in a joint statement that the supply would be on top of 50,000 tonnes of food being shipped to the troubled communist state by the South Korean Red Cross.
A spokesman of the groups said they would buy corn in China before delivering it to the North via the Red Cross, the only allowed delivery channel for the South Korean private sector.

Under an accord hammered out last month between the North and South Korean Red Cross societies, trains carrying the first shipments of the 50,000 tonnes of relief supplies arrived in the famine-threatened North on Thursday.
For the first time in 12 years, North Korea allowed South Korean Red Cross officials to visit the country to oversee the delivery.
The spokesman said the civic groups wanted the Red Cross to send the additional relief supplies by the end of July but transportation difficulties could delay the shipments.
